questions.question_text: What is the primary definition of conflict as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: A physical fight between two or more people
A disagreement or clash between differing opinions, needs, or goals
A situation where someone always wins and another loses
An unnatural occurrence that should be avoided at all costsCorrect Answer:B) A disagreement or clash between differing opinions, needs, or goals

questions.question_text: Why is conflict considered a natural part of relationships according to the chapter?

options.text: It shows that people don’t care about each other
It happens because no two people will always have the same views or needs
It only occurs in unhealthy relationships
It prevents relationships from growing strongerCorrect Answer:B) It happens because no two people will always have the same views or needs

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of an internal conflict as described in the chapter?

options.text: Arguing with a friend over weekend plans
Disagreeing with parents about curfew rules
Feeling torn between joining a new club or staying with a sports team
Having a dispute in a group chat over a misinterpreted commentCorrect Answer:C) Feeling torn between joining a new club or staying with a sports team

questions.question_text: What is a common cause of conflict among teens highlighted in the chapter?

options.text: Lack of interest in social activities
Miscommunication, especially over text or social media
Always agreeing with peers and family
Avoiding emotional discussionsCorrect Answer:B) Miscommunication, especially over text or social media

questions.question_text: How can emotions escalate a conflict, based on the chapter’s discussion?

options.text: By encouraging calm and thoughtful responses
By causing someone to use “I” statements to express feelings
By leading to impulsive reactions like blaming or yelling
By helping both parties understand each other’s perspectivesCorrect Answer:C) By leading to impulsive reactions like blaming or yelling

questions.question_text: What is an effective way to recognize and manage emotional triggers during a disagreement, according to the chapter?

options.text: Ignoring your feelings to avoid making the situation worse
Reflecting on past conflicts to identify patterns that provoke strong emotions
Immediately confronting the other person about their behavior
Pretending the trigger doesn’t exist to keep the peaceCorrect Answer:B) Reflecting on past conflicts to identify patterns that provoke strong emotions
